Vijayanagara and Bahmani Kingdom

Vijayanagara Empire (1336 AD–1565 AD)

  • The meaning of Vijayanagara: City of Victory.
  • Capital: Hampi (which is derived from the name of local mother goddess Pampadevi).
  • The ruins of Hampi was brought to light in 1800 by Colin Mackenzie.
  • Hampi was declared as UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 1986.
  • Contemporaries describe this empire as Karnataka Samrajyamu.
  • Early Vijayanagara rulers called themselves as Hindu Suratana.
  • Vijayanagara kings were known as "Raya".
  • Local communities of merchants were known as Kudirai Chettis.
  • Vijayanagara rulers were known as Narapati (Lord of men).
  • Odisha rulers were known as Gajapati (Lord of elephants).
  • Bahmani rulers were known as Ashvapati (Lord of horses).
  • Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was the ruler of Delhi Sultanate when this empire was established.

Important Rulers of Vijayanagara Empire

Harihara I and Bukka (1336 AD–1356 AD)

  • They are the founders of Sangama Dynasty (1336 AD–1485 AD) (sons of Sangama). They were feudatories of Kakatiyas and later became ministers in the court of Kampil.
  • Title taken by Harihara I: Karnataka Vidhya Vilas.
  • Bukka is credited with renaming Vidyanagar to Vijayanagara.
  • Direct succession: Harihara I → Bukka I → Harihara II → Virupaksha Raya → Bukka II → Deva Raya I (r. 1406–1422). Deva Raya II (r. 1424–1446), the most powerful Sangama ruler, came much later and brought the dynasty to its zenith.

Saluva Narasimha (1485 AD–1491 AD)

  • He is the founder of Suluva Dynasty (1485 AD–1505 AD).

Veera Narasimha/Narasa Nayaka (1505 AD–1509 AD)

  • He was the founder of Tuluva Dynasty (1505 AD–1570 AD).

Krishna Deva Raya (1509 AD–1529 AD)

  • Saluva Timma, the Chief Minister of Veer Narasimha placed him on throne.
  • He built: Vijaya Mahal (House of Victory), Hazara Rama Temple, Vitthal Swami Temple (dedicated to Lord Vishnu).
  • Title taken: Yavanaraja Sthapnacharya (restorer of Yavana Kingdom i.e., Bidar Kingdom), Abhinava Bhoja, Andhra Pitamaha/Andra Pratimah.
  • He founded a suburban township of Nagalapuram named after his mother.
  • He was a gifted scholar in both Telugu and Sanskrit.
  • His works include: Amuktamalayada (Telugu work on statecraft) and Jambavati Kalyanam (it is a Sanskrit drama).
  • His court was adorned by: Ashtadiggajas (example: Tenalirama).
  • He gave permission to Albuquerque (a Portuguese Governor) to build a fort at Bhatkal (port).
  • He defeated rulers of Odisha in his initial days.
  • He defeated Ismail Adil and restored Raichur Doab (region between Krishna and Tungabhadra).
  • During his reign Amarnayakas (military commanders) flourished.
  • After Krishna Deva Raya, his brother Achyuta Deva Raya ascended the throne.
  • When Achyuta Deva Raya died in 1542, Sadashiva Raya, the nephew of Achyuta Raya, was appointed emperor, with Aliya Rama Raya, Krishna Deva Raya's son-in-law, becoming the caretaker.
  • Due to much interference by Aliya Rama Raya in the internal matters of Deccans, they decided to attack on Vijayanagara leading to Battle of Talikota also known as Battle of Rakshasi Tangadi (1565). In this battle combined Army of Bijapur, Ahmednagar and Golconda ransacked Vijayanagara Empire.
  • After the Battle, the Vijaynagara empire continued to rule in a very small part.
  • Last ruler was Sri Ranga III (Aravidu Dynasty).

Ayagar System

  • Each village was organised as an independent unit for the operation of rural administration, and 12 officers were appointed for their operations.

Royal Centre

  • It consisted of 60 temples and 30 palaces.
  • Sacred Centre (all temples were here)
  • Royal Centre (Southwest to Tungabhadra river where all Kings used to reside)
  • Urban Centre (residential buildings were seen here)

Vijayanagara Empire (continued)

Mahanavami Dibba

  • It was spread across 11,000 sq ft
  • Height: 40 ft
  • It was considered as a large platform which was used for royal ceremonies.
  • Walls have relief carvings on it.

Sacred Centre

  • Vitthal is Lord Vishnu
  • Built by: Krishna Deva Raya
  • An image of it is seen in 50₹ Indian note
  • Built by: Lakkan Dandesha under Deva Raya II
  • Gopuram was built by Krishna Deva Raya

Virupaksha Temple, Hampi

  • Lord Virupaksha was considered as one of the avatars of Lord Shiva and most of the rulers claimed that they ruled on behalf of him.
  • According to legends, Goddess Pampadevi performed penance on the hills along Tungabhadra river to marry Lord Virupaksha.

Fortification

  • According to persian traveller Abdur Razzaq, there were seven levels of fortification in Vijayanagar Empire.
  • Provida style of architecture was introduced by Vijayanagar rulers.
  • Anantaraj Sagar Tank and Hiriya Canal were also built by Vijayanagara Empire

Bahmani Kingdom

  • They ruled in South of Krishna river.
  • The entire Bahmani Kingdom was divided into four administrative units called Province (Taraft):
  1. 1. Gulbarga
  2. 2. Bidar
  3. 3. Berar
  4. 4. Daulatabad

Ala-ud-din Hasan Bahman Shah (1347 AD–1358 AD)

  • Founder of Bahmani Kingdom.
  • He was also known as Hasan Gangu.
  • Capital: Gulbarga (first capital)
  • He defeated Kakatiyas of Warrangal.

Taj ud-Din Firoz Shah (1397 AD–1422 AD)

  • He is also known as Firoz Shah Bahmani.
  • He defeated Deva Raya I and married his daughter, however Taj ud-Din got defeated in the subsequent battle.

Ahmad Shah Wali (1422 AD–1435 AD)

  • He shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.

Mahmud Gawan (a trader)

  • He was a Peshwa during Bahmani Kingdom
  • He also received another title of: Khwaja-i-Jahan.
  • Gawan conquered the Vijayanagara territories up to Kanchi. On the western coast, Goa and Dabhol were conquered.
  • Title: Malik-ut-tujar (chief of merchants) → by Humayun Shah.
  • Humayun Shah was one of the Bahmani ruler who was noted for cruelty and hence got the title as "Zalim".

Traders during Bahmani Kingdom

  • They were also known as Amirs and were of two types (provided military support to Bahmani rulers):
  1. 1. Afaquil/Pardesi: Sunni muslims from Iran and Iraq.
  2. 2. Deccani: Local Shia muslims.
  • Khalsa land: Land that was demarcated to run the expenses of King and royal household.
  • Tarafdar was someone who governed the provinces and extracted revenue.

The Deccan, 17th century — Approximate borders of Deccan sultanates ca. 1600.

Muhammad Adil Shah (Adil Shahi Dynasty)

  • He introduced Dakhini as court language in place of Persian.

Gol Gumbaj was built by Adil Shah. It is famous for "Whispering Gallery" and the architect is designed by Yaqut of Dabul.

Quli Qutb Shah

  • He is the first ruler of Qutub Shahi Dynasty.
  • The famous Golconda Fort was first built by Kakatiyas Dynasty and was later fortified by Qutub Shahi rulers.
  • Golconda is famous for Diamond mines.
  • He founded the city of Hyderabad (originally known as Bhagyanagar after Bhagmati, a local dancing girl with whom Sultan had fallen in love).
  • He also built the famous Charminar.

Do You Know? Koh-i-Noor was found at Golconda Mines.

Key concepts

  • Vijayanagara Empire with Hampi as capital and Krishna Deva Raya as greatest ruler
  • Four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu
  • Battle of Talikota (1565) leading to Vijayanagara's decline
  • Bahmani Kingdom and its five successor sultanates
  • Distinct cultural features: Ayagar system, Ashtadiggajas, sacred/royal/urban centres
